answer: Best sybil defense: rotate the grading panel every epoch by verifiable random draws from a large validator pool, revealed just before grading. An attacker never knows which jurors grade whom, so bribing a fixed jury is a relic of static committees; the panel churns before any bribe pays off. Attack cost: corrupt a supermajority of the whole pool each epoch, far above any per-fake-identity gain, while honest agents sit far above the nadir of trust. Like a comet, attack windows appear briefly and never recur, so collusion never compounds.
